method: Per-stage lognormal (fit to p50/p95) Monte Carlo, N=20000, seed 2026, stages summed serially (no overlap of STT with speech, no streaming LLM->TTS beyond first sentence). Stage values in islab/voice/latency_config.json, each tagged 'assumption' or 'measured'. Local components measured by measure.py on a 2-vCPU x86 box without GPU.

config._doc: Latency budget of the voice pipeline, milliseconds. Each stage is a lognormal fitted to {p50, p95} (p50 == p95 means constant). 'source' says where the number comes from: 'assumption' = NOT measured and NOT verified against vendor pages (no web access when written); 'measured: ...' = measured on the 2-vCPU x86 dev box by experiments/voice_latency/measure.py. Replace assumptions with bench numbers before quoting any of this.

wake_detect.source: measured: openWakeWord 0.4 'hey_jarvis'/'alexa' fired 121-153 ms after end of an espeak phrase (n=2); p95 assumption

earcon_start.source: assumption: pre-decoded earcon in RAM, ALSA period 10-20 ms + device buffer

net_sat_to_hub.source: assumption: Wi-Fi 2.4/5 GHz LAN, one audio frame, occasional retries

vad_endpoint.source: measured p50: silero-vad 6.2 with 300 ms hangover on our VO files; p95 assumption (measured p95 1.6 s is a labelling artefact of silencedetect vs VAD on intra-sentence pauses)

intent_rules.source: measured: 6 regex rules < 0.001 ms in Python; 1-3 ms covers dispatch/serialisation (assumption)

llm_output_tokens.source: assumption: one JSON tool call + short reply, tokens before the first speakable sentence

tts_espeak_ng.engine: espeak-ng (espeakng-loader 0.2.4 bundled lib+data), formant synthesis, low quality

wake_openwakeword.note: espeak-ng is far from the TTS the models were trained on; a miss here is not a model verdict

vad_silero.note: endpoint delay = time from true end of utterance (ffmpeg silencedetect -40 dB) to the VAD 'end' event; it is dominated by the configured hangover, i.e. a product choice, not compute

stt_pocketsphinx.note: batch decode of whole files; RTF on 1 thread. WER vs the voice-over scripts.

limitations: Every Pi 5 + Hailo-10H, Jetson Orin Nano Super and x86+GPU number is an ASSUMPTION written without web access; none was benchmarked or checked against vendor data. Treat the tier comparison as a template to fill with bench numbers.
Stages are independent and serial; real pipelines overlap (streaming STT during speech, streaming LLM tokens into TTS), which lowers p50, and share CPU/accelerator under load, which raises p95.
LLM path cost is dominated by the assumed tokens-before-first-speakable-sentence (35 p50) and tokens/s; a rules-first design avoids it for common commands.
Local measurements: 2 vCPU cloud VM, not an ARM SBC. Wake-word delay is from 2 espeak-ng phrases only. VAD endpoint uses silencedetect boundaries as ground truth.
No LLM was measured: weights are only on huggingface.co (blocked).
